subject: Admin activity evidence: schema, filtering, and export playbook

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jansen <alex.jansen@greenlake.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Admin activity evidence: schema, filtering, and export playbook

Alex / GreenLake security team —

Thanks for the list you sent over (attached). To move quickly for your SOC 2 Type II review, we want to propose a scoped export and a short runbook so your auditors can validate fidelity without pulling unnecessary PII. High-level asks from your side: what fields are mandatory for your auditors, timeframe (90 days vs 1 year), and preferred transport (S3 presigned vs SFTP vs signed manifest).

We’ll own producing a signed, integrity-checked bundle and a brief manifest that maps each logged field to the exported column. Below are the internal folks I’m looping in to align on: Karthik for schema & export tooling; Marissa for legal/redaction; Logan for storage & keys.

Deliverables proposed:
- A CSV schema for the admin activity rows (attached: admin_schema_v1.csv).
- Export modes: full snapshot (S3 presigned, gzipped, envelope-encrypted), streaming audit view (temporary read-only S3 signed URL), or filtered per-tenant differential exports.
- Manifest: HMAC-SHA256 per file, signed with our export key; signed statement of retention windows and sampling (if partial).

Questions for you before we finalize:
1) Which timeframe do you need material for the audit window? (90/180/365 days)
2) Are you okay with field-level redaction for attendee/display_name and email hash instead of full addresses?
3) Do you require timezone-normalized timestamps (UTC) or original event timezone?

Attaching: evidence_requirements_greentlake.pdf (your list).

—
Olga Petrov
Senior Security & Compliance PM
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Jansen <alex.jansen@greenlake.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Admin activity evidence: schema, filtering, and export playbook

Olga / Alex —

Quick draft mapping attached (admin_schema_v1.csv). Key points from implementation perspective: we already capture the following event classes in operator/admin logs — session_start/stop, console_auth_attempt, role_change, key_rotation, model_deploy, config_patch, route_override, KV-cache-evict, and operator-impersonation. For each event we emit: event_id (uuid), timestamp_utc, operator_id (internal id), actor_display (string), actor_email_hash (sha256), tenant_id, event_type, target_resource, before/after_blob (json-string, redacted), request_id, trace_id, and retention_label.

Export options (pros/cons):
- Full snapshot (recommended for small windows): Produces per-day gzipped CSVs, envelope-encrypted with customer KMS when requested. Manifest includes HMAC-SHA256 + size + file list. Good for auditor ingest.
- Differential per-tenant exports: Allows GreenLake to request a tenant slice (start/end). Reduces PII exposure but requires careful deduping across windows.
- Streaming / live view: Read-only temporary S3 signed URLs into a sanitized view; useful for small ad-hoc queries but harder to reproduce for audit attestation.

Redaction patterns I recommend: hash emails + mask last 2 chars of display names, redact IPs unless explicitly requested by legal, and include a mapping table only if a non-disclosure and custodian request is signed.

Operational notes:
- We keep operator logs at 13 months by default (cold storage after 90 days).
- For signed manifests we use an export key rotated monthly and rotate HMAC keys quarterly.
- We can provide timezone-normalized UTC timestamps and also include original tz offset column for provenance.

I will attach a sample 7-day export layout by EOD.

—Karthik
Director, Inference Ops
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Jansen <alex.jansen@greenlake.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T15:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Admin activity evidence: schema, filtering, and export playbook

Folks —

Couple of legal / compliance notes from my side before we finalize the export method:

1) Sampling vs full-window: For SOC 2 materiality, auditors often want reproducible full-window exports. If GreenLake is comfortable with a certified sampling approach, we need an agreed sampling protocol (seed, deterministic selection, and manifest). Otherwise plan for full exports for the audit window.

2) PII handling: If we hash emails, include the salt description and an access path for a sealed escrow (only accessible under legal process). We should avoid reversible redaction unless customer signs a data-access addendum.

3) Chain-of-custody: manifest must include a timestamped handoff record (who requested, who exported, storage checksum, and a DocuSign link or signed statement). If GreenLake needs notarization we can add the attestation block.

4) Retention: We should confirm GreenLake’s required retention. Our default retention policy is 13 months (hot 90d, cold archived). If they request >13 months we’ll need an exception and contract amendment.

I support Karthik’s recommendation of HMAC per-file + file-level envelope encryption. Also document the owner (SRE export job id) so auditors can tie the manifest to the pipeline run.

On attachments: I reviewed your evidence_requirements_greentlake.pdf and noted they expect timestamps normalized and clear field-level descriptions; good that we’ll include the before/after_blob redaction notes.

—Marissa Cole
Legal Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
